candidates.choice: Whether FakeEnvironment's documented 'always separator-terminated' guarantee for GetBaseDirectory() must hold when the baseDirectory argument is left at its default (falls back to home), or is understood to hold only when a caller explicitly passes an already-terminated string.
candidates.forcedBy: Building FakeEnvironment.Create per the contract's own 'What to do' step 3 (baseDirectory defaults to home, following the existing current/temp pattern) silently produces a non-terminated GetBaseDirectory() for every one of today's call sites that omit baseDirectory — SystemServicesBuilder.Fake() (Host.Home), CliMachine.RunWithInput, and ProcessArchitectureTests — because Host.Home is EnvironmentAdapter.GetHomeDirectory() -> Environment.GetFolderPath(SpecialFolder.UserProfile), which is not separator-terminated on typical POSIX/Windows values (e.g. '/Users/tester', '/home/runner'). No acceptance check exercises this default path: the separator unit test in acceptance #8 exercises an explicit FakeEnvironment.Create(...) call, and the OS-agnostic test in item 6 uses SystemServicesBuilder.Real(), not Fake(). Left alone, the shared Fake() builder — the one used almost everywhere in the suite — diverges from the just-decided real-adapter invariant (Decision 5) with nothing to catch it, so any future production code exercising GetBaseDirectory() under the standard fake harness gets a silently wrong (non-terminated) value that passes today's tests.
candidates.evidence: Decision 5 (contract lines 13, 79) states the fake 'reproduces a separator-terminated value'; contract 'What to do' step 3 (line 49) directs baseDirectory to default to home 'following the existing pattern'; tests/AgentGuard.TestHelpers/SystemServicesBuilder.cs:245-252 and 294-305 (Host.Home = real GetHomeDirectory(), no baseDirectory passed to FakeEnvironment.Create); tests/AgentGuard.Cli.Tests/CliMachine.cs:107-108 and tests/AgentGuard.Tests/ProcessArchitectureTests.cs:88-93 (same omission); tests/AgentGuard.TestHelpers/FakeEnvironment.cs:85 (`baseDirectory ?? home` with no normalization).

candidates.choice: Which owned primitive the new OS-agnostic accessor test (What-to-do step 6 / Acceptance 6) uses to prove GetBaseDirectory() 'returns a non-empty path to a directory that exists' — the contract names two interchangeably ('checked through the owned IFileReader/directory reader') but they are not interchangeable for a directory path.
candidates.forcedBy: System.IO.File.Exists() — the BCL primitive IFileReader.Exists wraps verbatim (FileReaderAdapter.cs:25: `public bool Exists(string path) => File.Exists(path);`) — is documented by .NET to return false, never throw, when given a path that is a directory rather than a file. If the test reaches for IFileReader (the name the contract states first) to assert the base directory 'exists', the assertion is checking the wrong predicate: a real, existing base directory makes File.Exists return false, so the test either fails for a reason unrelated to the bug it's meant to catch, or gets written to assert the (misleading) false result, defeating the acceptance check. The correct owned primitive is IFileSystem.GetDirectoryReader() -> IDirectoryEnumerator.DirectoryExists(path), which wraps Directory.Exists and is the one BCL call that answers 'is this a directory' correctly.
candidates.evidence: contract-linux-policy-path.md 'What to do' item 6 and Acceptance item 6 ('...checked through the owned IFileReader/directory reader'); src/AgentGuard.CrossPlatform/FileReaderAdapter.cs:25 (Exists wraps File.Exists); src/AgentGuard.Abstractions/Contracts/IFileSystem.cs:41 (GetDirectoryReader() -> IDirectoryEnumerator) and IDirectoryEnumerator.cs:19 (DirectoryExists wraps Directory.Exists) — the correctly-typed owner the contract's phrasing leaves as an unstated pick.

findings.choice: Whether FakeEnvironment's decided 'separator-terminated GetBaseDirectory()' guarantee (Decision 5) must hold in the default case where baseDirectory falls back to home — i.e. must the fake normalize the home fallback to terminated, or only faithfully return whatever seed it is given.
findings.whyForced: Unaddressed, the code ships as written: FakeEnvironment.Create does `baseDirectory ?? home` with no normalization (line 85), and every default call site — SystemServicesBuilder.Fake(), CliMachine, ProcessArchitectureTests — omits baseDirectory, so GetBaseDirectory() silently returns an unterminated home path (e.g. /Users/tester) for the shared fake harness.
findings.howItBites: The Fake() builder is used across almost the whole suite and omits baseDirectory, so its GetBaseDirectory() violates the documented terminated-value guarantee — a value the real AppContext.BaseDirectory can never emit. No test catches it: acceptance #8 exercises only an explicit Create(...), and the OS-agnostic test uses Real(). Any future code that relies on the terminated invariant (string-concatenating a filename onto GetBaseDirectory() instead of Path.Combine) builds a wrong path under the most-used fake harness while every test passes, then behaves differently against the real adapter — a latent, hard-to-trace fake-vs-real divergence in the primary test double.
options: Normalize inside the fake: always store a trailing-separator-terminated base directory (including the home fallback) so GetBaseDirectory() is unconditionally terminated, matching the real adapter's invariant; extend acceptance #8 to also assert the DEFAULT (no baseDirectory passed) path is terminated.

Leave the fake faithful/raw: home default stays unterminated, require any test needing termination to pass a terminated string explicitly, and weaken Decision 5's guarantee to 'only when explicitly seeded'.
Drop the home default for baseDirectory: make the fake's base directory a required argument so it can never silently emit a value the real primitive could not produce.
findings.recommended: Option 1 — normalize the stored base directory (home default included) to terminated and extend acceptance #8 to cover the default path; terminating reproduces the primitive's own invariant rather than adding policy, so it honors the already-decided guarantee everywhere and closes the test gap.
